Peter Whewell now returning to form after a few months lay off when on the Continent during the Summer set about retrieving our lost fortunes and with a steady run took us up to 15th during which he caught Chris Steer who was running for the B team and having one of his off days.
His struggling effort left him over two minutes behind our first man, Peter Whewell, and dangerously near that old Belgrave favourite, Jack Brown.

We say farewell to Peter Whewell who returned to South Africa the day after the 'National'. During his stay here he worked for a firm of auditors, and it was the frequent spells of late working and consequent lack of training that led to his loss of form between arrival and departure.

It will be up to our three under-24's Bicourt, Major and Donnison to share an ever increasing degree of responsibility in our future teams, especially with the loss of Peter Whewell to South Africa, Gerry Williams to Venezuela, Chris Steer to Canada and Geoff North to retirement (again).

PETER WHEWELL sends best wishes to the Club from Johannesburg and writes, "I have been receiving The Belgravian each quarter and it is good to see that most of the fellows I ran with are still competing.

PETER WHEWELL, who played a large part in many of our team successes a few years ago, writes from South Africa to say that he hopes to be back in England this December for a short period and looks forward to renewing old acquaintances.
